AUDIT COMPLETE on x86 host with no board. Headline: every arithmetic operator GDN needs is natively supported (CumSum -> ArmCumulate, delta rule -> ArmMatMul/ArmEltwise, causal conv -> ArmDepthwiseConv), but the sequential recurrence is NOT expressible - Scan rejected outright, Loop accepted only with a compile-time-constant trip count via silent static unrolling (no loop survives in the IR), Loop with runtime trip count rejected ('Graph is not DAG'). Empirically confirms the CPU-first mapping: keeping the scan on CPU is not a preference, the NPU has no construct for it. Also surfaced two undocumented environment facts (cixbuilder wheel is cp310-only; cixparse imports tensorflow even for ONNX). Written up in docs/FINDINGS.md 1 with logs committed under artifacts/npu_op_probe/audit/. Caveat: frontend lowering only - per-op NPU-vs-CPU placement and throughput still need full cixbuild and on-device runs (ob-8xc).

ADR 0003 written. Primary Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, fallback Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, decided against config.json read directly from HF rather than the survey summary. Confirmed from primary source: 4B is 32 layers = exactly 24 GDN + 8 full attention with an explicit layer_types array, hidden 2560, 262144 native context, 16/32 linear key/value heads, 128/128 head dims, conv kernel 4. Computed the memory decomposition: GDN state 48MB flat at every context length vs KV cache 128MB@4K rising to 8GB@262K, and an all-full-attention counterfactual of ~32.8GB at 262K, so the hybrid saves ~24.8GB (75%) on a 64GB board. Caught and corrected a figure I had been repeating: the 4B has 32 value heads so its per-layer state is 524,288 floats, not the 262,144 from the GDN-2 paper's 1.3B config. One assumption flagged as open: the n_v_heads x d_k x d_v layout still needs confirming from modeling code (ob-37v).

bench/manifest.py implemented. capture() / write() / manifest_ref() plus a __main__ that dumps the current machine's manifest. Stdlib-only (imports cleanly in the NOE 3.10 env and on the board). docs/METRICS.md written - operational definitions for the whole frozen metric vocabulary, such that two people measuring independently get comparable numbers.

Load-bearing timer decisions: t_submit (prompt handed to an already-warm model) is the shared origin, so model load and JIT are never inside any metric; TTFT INCLUDES tokenization since the schema calls it user-facing, while prefill_tokens_per_sec EXCLUDES it (forward-pass invocation to last-position logits) so the two answer different questions; token 1 belongs to PREFILL not decode, since it comes from the prefill pass's own last-position logits, making decode's numerator N-1 over a single wall-clock span rather than a mean of per-step rates.

Statistical defaults: 3 discarded warmups; 30 repeats for headline numbers at 4K/32K, 10 minimum at 128K/262K, never below 5; p50 and p95 mandatory with p99 explicitly NOT mandated because at N=10-30 a p99 is indistinguishable from reporting the max, which the project prohibits; two configs differ only if |delta p50| exceeds 2x the larger spread AND their p50-p95 ranges do not overlap.

Memory is never derived from RSS (which cannot separate the three components) but from model introspection plus config-derived formulas.

Corrected after the fact: the agent was launched before ADR 0003 fixed the state size, so it used 262,144 elements/layer. Patched to the 4B's 524,288 (96 MiB/token across 24 GDN layers, ceiling ~993 tok/s from state traffic). Its central conclusion survived unchanged - arithmetic intensity is 0.25 FLOP/byte for BOTH checkpoints, because MACs and bytes both scale with state size, which makes the bandwidth-bound argument a structural property of the rank-1 update rather than an artefact of one model's dimensions.

Complete on main: docs/GDN_LAYER_AUDIT.md (220 lines) and docs/GDN_ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md (281 lines), both traced to modeling_qwen3_5.py and modular_qwen3_5.py rather than secondary sources. Covers everything the bead asked for: layer placement read from the explicit layer_types array (full-attention at indices {3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31} for the 4B, {3,7,11,15,19,23} for the 0.8B - read directly, not inferred from the interval), causal depthwise Conv1D, decay gating, the delta-rule update, chunk size, head dimensions, and the linear:full ratio. Critically it CONFIRMS the recurrent state shape that was previously only assumed: the state is allocated as torch.zeros(batch_size, num_heads, k_head_dim, v_head_dim), i.e. (batch, n_value_heads, d_k, d_v) - a rank-2 matrix per head, not a vector. 4B: (1,32,128,128) = 524,288 elements = 2.0 MiB/layer. 0.8B: (1,16,128,128) = 262,144 = 1.0 MiB/layer. That resolves the open question flagged in the gdn-state-size memory and validates ADR 0003's assumption.

Policy recorded in docs/adr/0006-quantization-policy.md: INT4 weights, recurrent state FP32, decay/beta gates FP16, KV cache FP16, with the per-tensor table and the reasoning for the state carve-out (error feeds back through every step rather than staying local, unlike a KV cache). Amended 2026-08-04 with the first cross-device narrow-format data from ob-8qt.4: software bf16 negates the bandwidth win on A76-class cores (1.10x at 4B, slower than fp32 at 0.8B), so prefer FP16 there; BF16 pays only with hardware support (Armv8.6-A+, including the O6's A720) or on cores slow enough to amortize conversion. Consequence: the narrow format must be selected at RUNTIME from the ISA rather than compiled in - isa_detect.py already reports bf16 and asimdhp. Headline decision unchanged; weight quantization remains the dominant lever at ~95-99% of decode bandwidth.

Cross-device mixed-precision measurement complete, cherry-picked from bench/t4 commit 936576d (the rest of PR #14 is superseded and must not be merged - it would delete main's harness, fleet_analysis, optimized kernels and prompt corpus). First data on a second core class: RK3588 A76 big / A55 little, hardware fp16 but no hardware bf16, exercising the software conversion path. Every figure verified against the committed CSVs to 0.1us. gated_scan state narrowing stays flat at prefill on all three core classes (<=6%), confirming it as a decode/residency lever; fp16 output narrowing is a portable 1.45-1.59x win via single-cycle FCVTN; and software bf16 negates the win on the FASTEST core (1.10x at 4B on A76, slower than fp32 at 0.8B - 129.5 vs 124.0us, spreads 1.1%/2.6%, so real). ADR 0006 amended. Caveat: A55 little-cluster rows carry 41-81% spreads and are not quotable individually.

Obsoleted by an architecture change rather than fixed-and-shipped. The maintainer is replacing the N-independent-agents-per-node model with ONE orchestrator agent on a loop holding access to all nodes, so the per-node goose loop that this bug describes is being retired. The underlying fix still landed and is still correct (docs/agent-task.template.md plus ensure_task() in goose-loop.sh regenerate a deleted task file), and it stays useful for any future per-node loop, but there is no longer a fleet of loops to keep alive. The generalizable lesson is captured in the new orchestration beads: a device runner must never depend on an untracked file that a rebase can delete. Note the root cause was self-inflicted - my own repo-hygiene commit untracked .goose-task.md (necessarily, it held a credential) and that deletion propagated to any node that rebased.
